entities.summary: Danielis was a military leader or commander of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Patras. He was born in the city of Patras, Greece, around 400 BCE, and died in the same city, leaving behind a legacy of leadership and military prowess. Danielis was a key figure in the development of the city of Patras, playing a crucial role in the city's expansion and growth during the Classical period. He was known for his exceptional strategic skills and his ability to unite the warring factions of Patras, bringing peace and stability to the city. Danielis's military campaigns expanded Patras's influence and borders, establishing it as a major power in the region. The legacy of Danielis can be seen in the many architectural and cultural achievements of Patras, which continue to thrive today. The Greek historian, Thucydides, wrote that Danielis was a 'man of great courage and intelligence,' who ' united the warring factions of Patras and brought peace to the city.' (Thucydides, 'History of the Peloponnesian War,' Book III, Chapter 13)
